title: Timeline Corrupt Classification and Final Publication-Ledger Integration
released_boundary: InvestigationTimelineCanonicalHistoryBoundary — a typed timeline reconstruction service that consumes final publication operation evidence and other supported producer domains, distinguishes verified, corrupt, unverified, missing, and unsupported source states truthfully, preserves operation identity and producer evidence, and emits deterministic future PostgreSQL/DuckDB projection contracts.
consumer_purpose: Later Gridline history surfaces and PostgreSQL timeline materialization can expose governed work as trustworthy user-visible history rather than a best-effort narrative assembled from incompatible or mislabeled evidence.

defects_repaired.description: Four of five verifiers returned PARSED_UNVERIFIED when a supplied producer digest existed but recomputation failed. A known digest mismatch is corrupt/tampered evidence, not merely unverified.
defects_repaired.fix: Changed return value on digest mismatch in verify_coordination_event, verify_disclosure_event, verify_publication_event, and verify_checkpoint_event from PARSED_UNVERIFIED to CORRUPT.
defects_repaired.verified: 7 source_verification tests and 3 adapter tests confirm CORRUPT on mismatch across all 5 domains

defects_repaired.description: Coordination verifier double-encoded payload (_compact_json(_compact_json(payload))) making hash matches practically impossible, silently degrading all coordination events.
T1.2 adds operation_id for exactly-once deduplication. Timeline needed to carry this identity to distinguish retried operations from separate actions.
defects_repaired.fix: Added operation_id field to InvestigationTimelineEvent model. Publication adapter extracts operation_id from event envelope and preserves it in timeline events.
defects_repaired.verified: Integration test with real T1.2 ledger confirms operation_id preserved through adapter; test_adapt_publication_preserves_operation_id passes

T1.2_integration_verified.title: Publication Operation Identity and Concurrency-Safe Canonical Ledger Closure
tests_passed: Real T1.2 ledger consumed successfully (successful + refused events)
Retry deduplication: same operation_id → 1 ledger row → 1 timeline event
Distinct operations with identical output → 2 separate timeline events

updated_adapters: Publication adapter now reads operation_id from event envelope top-level
updated_verifiers: verify_observability_event: CORRUPT on mismatch (was already correct)
verify_coordination_event: CORRUPT on mismatch (was PARSED_UNVERIFIED), fixed double-encoding
postgresql_update: Added operation_id column (TEXT nullable) and idx_timeline_operation_id index
content_light_guarantee: Maintained. operation_id is a caller-supplied string (no raw content). All new fields are hashes, booleans, or enum values.
